claim: The SPI system uses a GFP-binding protein (GBP) derived from an alpaca antibody.
source: The SPI system uses a GFP-binding protein (GBP) derived from an alpaca antibody (Rothbauer et al., 2006), which when fused to a target protein of interest creates binary associations in vivo with GFP-tagged proteins (Rothbauer et al., 2006; Rothbauer et al., 2008; Grallert et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by citations to prior work (Rothbauer et al., 2006).

claim: GBP fused to a target protein creates binary associations in vivo with GFP-tagged proteins.
source: The SPI system uses a GFP-binding protein (GBP) derived from an alpaca antibody (Rothbauer et al., 2006), which when fused to a target protein of interest creates binary associations in vivo with GFP-tagged proteins (Rothbauer et al., 2006; Rothbauer et al., 2008; Grallert et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated and supported by multiple citations (Rothbauer et al., 2006; Rothbauer et al., 2008; Grallert et al., 2013).

claim: 23 different target proteins representing 18 major cellular compartments were chosen for the study.
source: We chose 23 different target proteins that represent 18 of the major cellular compartments (Figure 1A and Figure 1—source data 1), such as the nucleus (Pus1 and Rad52), the cell membrane (Psr1), and the endoplasmic reticulum (Sec63).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and references Figure 1A and source data.

claim: 98% of GBP–GFP combinations (129,098 out of 131,882) do not affect the growth of cells.
source: We expected that many of the forced associations would disrupt cellular homeostasis, but unexpectedly, we found that 98% of GBP–GFP combinations (129,098 out of 131,882) do not affect the growth of cells (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated with specific numerical data and references Figure 1C.

claim: Cells are surprisingly permissive for most protein-protein interactions.
source: These data imply that cells are surprisingly permissive for most protein-protein interactions and as a corollary that cells are broadly tolerant of proteins being relocated within the cell.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the data showing that 98% of combinations do not affect growth.

claim: Cells are broadly tolerant of proteins being relocated within the cell.
source: These data imply that cells are surprisingly permissive for most protein-protein interactions and as a corollary that cells are broadly tolerant of proteins being relocated within the cell.
evidence: The claim is an inference drawn from the observation that most forced protein associations do not affect growth.

claim: Approximately 72% of interactions result in detectable protein colocalization.
source: In cases where fluorescent imaging was able to detect protein relocalization, we confirmed that ~72% of interactions do occur.
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated and based on microscopy data analysis.

claim: 552 GBP-GFP combinations were examined using live cell imaging.
source: We examined 552 GBP-GFP combinations - each of the 23 GBP-tagged target proteins separately combined with a random selection of 24 GFP-tagged query proteins - using live cell imaging (Figure 2—source data 1, for examples see Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is directly stated with specific numbers and references to figures and source data.

claim: Of 314 GBP-GFP combinations where proteins were not already in the same compartment, 225 were detectably colocalized.
source: Of the 524 GBP-GFP combinations that we could score, 210 (40%) are already in the same compartment and so we cannot determine whether GFP and GBP associate, of the remaining 314, 225 were detectably colocalized (Figure 2C), indicating that in the majority of cases the protein-protein associations do occur (Figure 2, Figure 2—figure supplement 1 and Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated with specific numerical data and references to figures.

claim: Most synthetic protein-protein interactions do not cause a growth defect.
source: These observations are therefore consistent with the notion that most synthetic protein-protein interactions do not cause a growth defect.
evidence: The claim is an inference drawn from the colocalization data and growth data.

claim: There are roughly equal instances of the GBP protein recruiting the GFP protein as the reverse.
source: The image data support this notion; where it is possible to distinguish the location of two proteins in the cell, we observed that there are roughly equal instances of the GBP protein recruiting the GFP protein as the reverse (Figure 3 and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is based on analysis of microscopy images showing direction of protein movement.

claim: Structural components more often recruit proteins to their location than enzymes that are not anchored to a specific location.
source: However, this generalization is not true for some classes/types of proteins. When we look at individual GBP or GFP proteins, we find that structural components more often recruit proteins to their location than enzymes that are not anchored to a specific location (Figure 3, Figure 3—figure supplement 1 and Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is based on analysis of microscopy data showing differential recruitment patterns.

claim: Constitutive recruitment of a nucleosome remodeler to chromatin results in Hta2-GBP no longer being restricted to the nucleus.
source: An example of the latter is the recruitment of the nucleosome remodeling protein, Spt6, to the histone subunit Hta2. Constitutive recruitment of a nucleosome remodeler to the chromatin might be expected to give a phenotype and indeed we find that the histone subunit Hta2-GBP is strikingly no longer restricted to the nucleus (Figure 2E) concomitant with a strong growth defect.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by microscopy data in Figure 2E.

claim: The Hta2-Spt6 interaction results in a strong growth defect.
source: Constitutive recruitment of a nucleosome remodeler to the chromatin might be expected to give a phenotype and indeed we find that the histone subunit Hta2-GBP is strikingly no longer restricted to the nucleus (Figure 2E) concomitant with a strong growth defect.
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated and based on growth measurements.

claim: Around 2% of the forced interactions restrict growth.
source: Around 2% of the forced interactions restrict growth (Figure 1C, 4A and Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated with reference to figures showing growth data.

claim: Approximately 3% of interactions with validated GFP strains restrict growth.
source: However, we note that of the 6000 GFP-tagged proteins used in this study, only ~4000 have been validated and are clearly observable (Huh et al., 2003). We therefore reanalyzed the proteome-wide data using only 3905 GFP strains with unambiguous fluorescence signal (Tkach et al., 2012) and find that ~3% restrict growth (Figure 4—source data 1), consistent with the notion that most protein-protein associations do not restrict growth.
evidence: The claim is based on reanalysis of data using only validated GFP strains, with citations to prior work.

claim: 2784 SPIs were confirmed in total produced by 727 GFP-tagged query proteins with one or more of the 23 target proteins.
source: Using this approach, we confirmed 2784 SPIs in total produced by 727 GFP-tagged query proteins with one or more of the 23 target proteins (Figure 4—figure supplement 2 and Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated with specific numbers and references to figures.

claim: 75 GFP query proteins produce SPIs with at least 10 of the 23 GBP-tagged target proteins.
source: When we examine all the 727 SPI query proteins collectively (Figure 4A), we find that 75 GFP query proteins produce SPIs with at least 10 of our 23 GBP-tagged target proteins (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated with specific numbers and references to figures.

claim: Frequent SPI query proteins are on average of lower abundance than less frequent SPI query proteins.
source: These 'frequent SPI query proteins' are on average of lower abundance than less frequent SPI query proteins (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B,C), also they are enriched for essential genes (≈83%) and for proteins whose gene ontology (GO) terms include RNA metabolism (p-value = 9.26x10-5), mRNA polyadenylation (p-value = 1.63x10-9), cytoplasmic and nuclear transport (p-values = 1.14x10-8 and 1.69x10-7, respectively), microtubule nucleation (p-value = 5.09x10-8), and spindle pole body (p-value = 3.22x10-8).
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated with statistical data and references to figures.

claim: All 41 frequent SPIs from the Nuf2 screen are suppressed in heterozygous diploid cells.
source: Consistent with our expectation all 41 frequent SPIs are suppressed in heterozygous diploid cells, whereas 15% (6 out of 40) SPIs in the non-frequent group were reproduced in diploid cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated with specific numbers and references to a figure.

claim: 15% (6 out of 40) of non-frequent SPIs from the Nuf2 screen were reproduced in diploid cells.
source: Consistent with our expectation all 41 frequent SPIs are suppressed in heterozygous diploid cells, whereas 15% (6 out of 40) SPIs in the non-frequent group were reproduced in diploid cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated with specific numbers and references to a figure.

claim: Frequent SPI query proteins are predominantly those whose essential function is location-dependent.
source: Thus, we conclude that these frequent SPI query proteins are predominantly those whose essential function is location-dependent and whose sequestration to another compartment results in a growth defect (as is routinely achieved using other systems Haruki et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is a conclusion drawn from the diploid suppression data, with a citation to prior work.

claim: SPI screens using target proteins from the same cellular compartment give similar SPIs in specific cases.
source: Spearman's correlation coefficient analysis (Lubbock et al., 2013) indicates that, in specific cases, SPI screens using target proteins from the same cellular compartment give similar SPIs (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated with reference to statistical analysis and a figure.

claim: The Pus1 and Rad52 target proteins, which are both in the nucleus, produce SPIs with a similar set of query GFP proteins.
source: For example, the Pus1 and Rad52 target proteins, which are both in the nucleus, produce SPIs with a similar set of query GFP proteins.
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated as an example of similar SPIs from the same compartment.

claim: SPIs between query and target proteins that normally localize to the same cellular compartment are enriched (10.4% of confirmed SPIs vs. expected 7.1%, p-value = 1.8x10-9).
source: SPIs between query and target proteins that normally localize to the same cellular compartment are enriched (10.4% of our confirmed SPIs are with target and query proteins from the same compartment, versus an expected value of 7.1% for the full dataset, p-value = 1.8x10-9, Fisher's Exact test).
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated with specific percentages and statistical test results.

claim: SPIs with the nucleolar protein Nop10 are enriched for nucleolar components (21 out of 115, p-value = 1.8x10-8).
source: Also, this notion is true in specific cases, particularly for nuclear proteins. For example, SPIs with a nucleolar protein, Nop10, are enriched for nucleolar components (21 out of 115, p-value = 1.8x10-8, Fisher's exact test) or SPIs with the microtubule-associated kinetochore component Nuf2, which are enriched for microtubule components (described below).
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated with specific numbers and statistical test results.

claim: SPIs produced by proteins in different compartments tend to give a greater growth defect than those from the same compartments.
source: However, it should be noted that although there are more SPIs between proteins in the same compartment, SPIs produced by proteins in different compartments tend to give a greater growth defect (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated and references Figure 4C showing the data.

claim: SPI query proteins are enriched for characterized physical interactions compared with non-SPIs (p<2.2 x 10–16).
source: Unexpectedly, we find that SPI query proteins are enriched for characterized physical interactions, compared with non-SPIs (p<2.2 x 10–16, Wilcoxon's rank-sum).
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated with a specific p-value from a statistical test.

claim: Most SPI screens have a strong enrichment for genetic and physical interactions.
source: Most SPI screens have a strong enrichment for genetic and physical interactions indicating that the strongest SPIs share interactions (Figure 4E and Figure 4—figure supplement 5), which is a predictor of common function.
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated and references figures showing CLIK analysis.

claim: SPIs for the DNA repair protein Rad52 are enriched for components of the nuclear pore (p-value = 7x10-9).
source: For example, SPIs for the DNA repair protein Rad52 are enriched for components of the nuclear pore (Ndc1, Nic96, Nup1, Nup85, Nup49, Nup57, Nup84, Nup145, and Nup192; p-value = 7x10-9), specifically the Nup84 complex, which functions in specialized types of DNA repair (Nagai et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated with specific protein names, p-value, and citation.

claim: SPIs for the kinetochore protein Nuf2 are enriched for proteins involved in microtubule organization (p-value = 8x10-13).
source: Another example is the kinetochore protein Nuf2, whose SPIs are enriched for proteins involved in microtubule organization (Ark35, Bir1, Cbf2, Cdc14, Ctf19, Dad2, Dad4, Dsn1, Ipl1, Kip1, Kip3, Okp1, Spc24, Spc29, Spc42, Spc105, Spc110, Stu1, and Tub4; p-value = 8x10-13).
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated with specific protein names and p-value.

claim: Nuf2 is an outer kinetochore protein whose calponin-homology domain directs microtubule binding.
source: Nuf2 is an outer kinetochore protein whose calponin-homology domain directs microtubule binding (Wei et al., 2007; Ciferri et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated and supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Hmo1, Sgf29, and Sst2 all gave a strong SPI phenotype with the kinetochore protein Nuf2.
source: Hmo1, Sgf29 (both chromatin-associated proteins) and Sst2 (a GTPase activating protein) all gave a strong SPI phenotype with the kinetochore protein Nuf2.
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated based on SPI screen results.

claim: Only hmo1∆ gives a chromosomal instability phenotype among Hmo1, Sgf29, and Sst2 mutants.
source: Only one of these mutants, hmo1∆, gives a chromosomal instability phenotype (Stirling et al., 2011) and none have a reported role in kinetochore function.
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated and supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Hmo1, Sgf29, and Sst2 have no reported role in kinetochore function.
source: Only one of these mutants, hmo1∆, gives a chromosomal instability phenotype (Stirling et al., 2011) and none have a reported role in kinetochore function.
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated based on literature review.

claim: Hmo1 has SPIs with Nuf2, Mif2, and Ctf19, but not with Kre28, Mtw1, Dad2, Ctf3, Chl4, Skp1, Cnn1, or Cbf1.
source: We find that in addition to Nuf2, Hmo1 has SPIs with Mif2 and Ctf19, but not Kre28, Mtw1, Dad2, Ctf3, Chl4, Skp1, Cnn1, or Cbf1 (Figure 5A).
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated with specific protein names and references Figure 5A.

claim: The Hmo1 SPI is specific to central/outer kinetochore components.
source: These data suggest that the Hmo1 SPI is specific to central/outer kinetochore components.
evidence: The claim is an inference drawn from the specific pattern of SPIs observed.

claim: hmo1∆ and sgf29∆ cells have elevated levels of Dad4 outer kinetochore protein associated with their centromeres.
source: Strikingly, we find that hmo1∆ and, to a lesser extent, sgf29∆ cells both have elevated levels of Dad4 outer kinetochore protein associated with their centromeres, although the levels of Mtw1 were unaffected (Figure 5B,C and 5D).
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated and supported by fluorescence microscopy data in figures.

claim: The levels of Mtw1 were unaffected in hmo1∆ and sgf29∆ cells.
source: Strikingly, we find that hmo1∆ and, to a lesser extent, sgf29∆ cells both have elevated levels of Dad4 outer kinetochore protein associated with their centromeres, although the levels of Mtw1 were unaffected (Figure 5B,C and 5D).
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated and supported by fluorescence microscopy data in figures.

claim: Approximately one third of hmo1∆ cells have higher levels of Dad4 than those found in wild-type cells.
source: To test whether the hmo1∆ mutant was affecting Dad4 protein levels we quantified total cellular Dad4-YFP fluorescence in wild-type and mutant cells and find approximately one third of hmo1∆ cells have higher levels of Dad4 than those found in wild-type cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated and supported by quantitative fluorescence data.

claim: Nearly half of the hmo1∆ cells have Dad4 levels in the wild-type range.
source: Nearly half of the hmo1∆ cells have Dad4 levels in the wild-type range (+/- one standard deviation of the wild-type mean); hence cellular Dad4 protein levels are not sufficient to explain the aberrant Dad4 foci seen in most hmo1∆ cells (Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated and based on quantitative fluorescence analysis.

claim: Cellular Dad4 protein levels are not sufficient to explain the aberrant Dad4 foci seen in most hmo1∆ cells.
source: Nearly half of the hmo1∆ cells have Dad4 levels in the wild-type range (+/- one standard deviation of the wild-type mean); hence cellular Dad4 protein levels are not sufficient to explain the aberrant Dad4 foci seen in most hmo1∆ cells (Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is an inference drawn from comparing total cellular Dad4 levels with kinetochore foci intensity.

claim: Hmo1 is associated with purified kinetochores.
source: Furthermore, it has previously been shown that Hmo1 is associated with purified kinetochores (Akiyoshi et al., 2010), consistent with a direct role at the kinetochore.
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated and supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Hmo1 stimulates the activity of the SWI/SNF chromatin remodeling complex.
source: However, Hmo1 stimulates the activity of the SWI/SNF chromatin remodeling complex (Hepp et al., 2014) and therefore may affect expression of the DAD4 gene.
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated and supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: In specific cases SPIs define functional regulators.
source: These data support the notion that in specific cases SPIs define functional regulators.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion drawn from the Hmo1/Sgf29 kinetochore data.

claim: The histone subunits Hta2, Htb1, Htb2, and Hhf2 as well as the chromosomal proteins Bub1 and Mft1 have unique SPIs with the eisosome component Pil1.
source: For example, the histone subunits Hta2, Htb1, Htb2, and Hhf2 as well as the chromosomal proteins Bub1 and Mft1 have unique SPIs with the eisosome component Pil1.
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated based on SPI data analysis.

claim: Pil1 relocalizes from the plasma membrane in response to DNA damage.
source: These interactions may indicate a nuclear role for Pil1, which relocalizes from the plasma membrane in response to DNA damage (Tkach et al., 2012) and associates with histones and chromosomal proteins (Lambert et al., 2009; Akiyoshi et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated and supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Pil1 associates with histones and chromosomal proteins.
source: These interactions may indicate a nuclear role for Pil1, which relocalizes from the plasma membrane in response to DNA damage (Tkach et al., 2012) and associates with histones and chromosomal proteins (Lambert et al., 2009; Akiyoshi et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated and supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The Pil1-histone SPIs result from Pil1 recruitment into the nucleus.
source: Indeed, the Pil1-histone SPIs result from Pil1 recruitment into the nucleus (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated and supported by microscopy data in a figure.

claim: Query proteins from specific large functional complexes cluster together in hierarchical clustering analysis.
source: We find that query proteins from specific large functional complexes cluster together, for example, the mediator complex, which is involved in activating transcription, clusters together as do members of the COP1 coatomer, the outer ring of the nuclear pore, the signal recognition particle and TRAMP complex (Figure 4—figure supplement 6).
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated and supported by clustering analysis shown in figures.

claim: The mediator complex clusters together in SPI data.

claim: SPIs are not a substitute for physical interaction data.
source: It is important to note that SPIs are not a substitute for physical interaction data, but rather represent a common phenotype in response to forced association.
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated as an interpretation of what SPIs represent.

claim: SPIs represent a common phenotype in response to forced association.
source: It is important to note that SPIs are not a substitute for physical interaction data, but rather represent a common phenotype in response to forced association.
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated as a definition of what SPIs represent.

claim: Key sub-complexes within the kinetochore are clustered together purely based upon their 23 SPI scores.
source: We find that key sub-complexes within the kinetochore are clustered together purely based upon their 23 SPI scores (Figure 6).
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated and supported by clustering analysis shown in Figure 6.

claim: Three of the four members of the COMA complex cluster together (Ctf19, Okp1, and Mcm21).
source: For example, three of the four members of the COMA complex cluster together (Ctf19, Okp1, and Mcm21) with two members of the Ctf3 complex (Mcm22 and Nkp2), and Cse4 and Chl4, which are all part of the constitutive centromere associated network (CCAN) of inner kinetochore proteins that bind to centromeric DNA.
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated based on clustering analysis of kinetochore proteins.

claim: Three of the four MIND complex members (Dsn1, Nnf1, and Nsl1) cluster with Spc24, Kre28 and Nuf2.
source: Three of the four MIND complex members (Dsn1, Nnf1, and Nsl1) also cluster with Spc24, Kre28 and Nuf2, which are all part of the KMN network of outer kinetochore proteins.
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated based on clustering analysis of kinetochore proteins.

claim: The DAM/DASH complex segregates into distinct clusters with Dad2, 3, and 4 distinct from Dam1, Ask1, Dad1, Spc34, and Duo1.
source: In contrast, the DAM/DASH complex, which is composed of 10 different proteins, segregates into distinct clusters (with Dad2, 3, and 4 distinct from Dam1, Ask1, Dad1, Spc34, and Duo1).
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated based on clustering analysis of kinetochore proteins.

claim: Dad2, 3 and 4 are small central domain subunits of the DAM/DASH complex that are important for structural integrity of the complex.
source: Dad2, 3 and 4 are small central domain subunits of the DAM/DASH complex that are important for structural integrity of the complex and therefore potentially sensitive to association with other proteins (consequently they have many SPIs).
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated based on known structural information about the DAM/DASH complex.

claim: Dam1, Duo1, and Spc34 are key interaction hubs for the decameric DAM/DASH complex.
source: In contrast Dam1, Duo1, and Spc34 are key interaction hubs for the decameric complex (Shang et al., 2003) and Ask1's C-terminus plays an important role in intercomplex interactions (Ramey et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated and supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Ask1's C-terminus plays an important role in intercomplex interactions.
source: In contrast Dam1, Duo1, and Spc34 are key interaction hubs for the decameric complex (Shang et al., 2003) and Ask1's C-terminus plays an important role in intercomplex interactions (Ramey et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated and supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: SPI data correlate with the quaternary structure of the nuclear pore complex.
source: A similar correlation with the quaternary structure can be made for another large protein assembly, the nuclear pore complex (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated and supported by clustering analysis shown in a figure.

claim: SPIs indicate a common phenotype produced by specific protein-protein associations.
source: Hence, although SPIs do not substitute for physical interaction data they indicate a common phenotype produced by specific protein-protein associations.
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated as a conclusion about what SPIs represent.

claim: Cells have a remarkable and unanticipated tolerance for forced protein associations.
source: This analysis reveals that cells have a remarkable and unanticipated tolerance for forced protein associations, even if these associations lead to a proportion of the protein moving compartments within the cell.
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated in the abstract as a main finding.

claim: Cells are tolerant of forced protein associations even if these associations lead to a proportion of the protein moving compartments within the cell.

claim: The interactions that perturb growth provide a functional map of spatial protein regulation.
source: Furthermore, the interactions that do perturb growth provide a functional map of spatial protein regulation, identifying key regulatory complexes for the normal homeostasis of eukaryotic cells.
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated in the abstract as a main finding.

claim: SPIs identify key regulatory complexes for the normal homeostasis of eukaryotic cells.
